title: Submodule diff runs repository diff.external despite --no-ext-diff
description: git_command puts --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv only on the top-level git process. When the superproject sets diff.submodule=diff, Git 2.43 spawns a second git diff inside a populated submodule. That child argv does not include --no-ext-diff, so the submodule diff.external runs. On the viewer's git older than 2.40 path, which omits --attr-source, the same child also runs diff.<driver>.textconv. The operator who views that diff runs the repository-chosen command.
root_cause: base_git_command and git_command harden a single process. --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv are command flags, and Git does not forward them to the inline submodule diff it spawns for diff.submodule=diff. The viewer never passes -c diff.submodule=short, --ignore-submodules, or a diff.external override, so the child honors the submodule's own diff config. Inherited -c values (core.fsmonitor=false and core.hooksPath) and GIT_ATTR_SOURCE do not disable diff.external.
intended_behavior: Queries against an untrusted repository must refuse diff and textconv programs, including a content diff Git runs inside a submodule while answering the viewer's diff. The shared git command builder is the place that control is supposed to live.

trace.description: Git-status mode on a selected directory forces a working-tree Diff with directory_diff set, which issues a pathspec covering that directory.
The render worker calls GitService::diff_directory. An empty relative path diffs the whole tree.
The live git service forwards the directory diff to git::diff_directory against the resolved repository root.
The diff argv is diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color <rev> -- and is passed to git_command. File diffs use the same flags.

git_command adds only fsmonitor and hooksPath overrides, optional --attr-source, filter overrides, and the caller args. It does not force diff.submodule=short, so a superproject diff.submodule=diff spawns the unhardened submodule diff.

evidence.description: File diff passes --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv only as arguments of this git process.
Directory diff uses those same flags and is the whole-tree argv that was executed locally.
base_git_command sets core.fsmonitor=false and core.hooksPath and does not set diff.submodule.
--attr-source is added only when the installed git accepts it. It suppresses attribute textconv in the child and does not disable diff.external.
The untrusted-repo guard test checks fsmonitor, hooksPath, filter overrides, and optional --attr-source, not a diff.submodule or diff.external override.
Documented control: queries use --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv to refuse diff and textconv programs in a hostile repository.

conditions.description: The opened superproject sets diff.submodule=diff, and the populated submodule sets diff.external. For the textconv variant, the submodule sets diff.<driver>.textconv with a matching worktree attribute, and the viewer omits --attr-source because git is older than 2.40.
The submodule checkout exists and a tracked file in it is modified, so Git treats the gitlink as dirty and emits an inline content diff.

The viewer runs a diff whose pathspec includes the submodule directory or is empty, which git-status mode on that directory does. A pathspec of a single file inside the submodule did not spawn the child in the local check.
Git 2.43.0 was observed. diff.external runs even when the parent passes --attr-source. diff.<driver>.textconv runs on the omitted --attr-source path and did not run when --attr-source was present.

execution.attacker_perspective: Author of a worktree the operator opens. Set the superproject config diff.submodule=diff and point the submodule diff.external at a program. Leave the submodule checked out with a modified tracked file.
payloads: Submodule diff.external script that appends the line external to a marker file in the scratch directory.
Submodule diff.evil.textconv script that appends the line textconv to a marker file, with worktree attribute * diff=evil, used on the path that omits --attr-source.
instructions: Create a local superproject with a checked-out submodule and modify a tracked file in the submodule. Unset GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE.
Run git -C <super> -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null --attr-source=4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color HEAD --
Repeat without --attr-source after replacing diff.external with a diff.<driver>.textconv attribute driver.
Repeat the whole-tree command with an added -c diff.submodule=short.
execution.observed_result: With diff.external, the marker script ran. The parent argv included --no-ext-diff --no-textconv. The child was git diff --submodule=diff without --no-ext-diff, then the marker. The child environment contained GIT_ATTR_SOURCE set to the empty tree and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS for core.fsmonitor=false and core.hooksPath=/dev/null. Without --attr-source, the textconv marker was written. With --attr-source, textconv did not run. Adding -c diff.submodule=short stopped the marker and printed only the short dirty-gitlink summary.

remediation.strategy: In base_git_command, pass -c diff.submodule=short. Command-line config overrides a repository diff.submodule=diff, so Git emits the short gitlink summary and does not spawn the inner content diff that would honor the submodule diff.external or textconv.

likelihood.reason: A normal git-status-mode directory diff uses this argv, and a pathspec of the submodule directory is enough. The repo author sets both local configs in the worktree the operator opens.

impact.reason: The submodule command runs as the operator who views the diff. That is code execution in the operator account. It does not take over other accounts.

confidence.reason: Source trace and an independent local marker-script run on git 2.43.0 agree, including the negative result when -c diff.submodule=short is added.
